test.originality_statement: Every question below is original. None reproduces an official ESAT, NSAA, or ENGAA question.

questions.question_text_markdown: \(ABCD\) is a square of side \(12\text{ cm}\). The points \(E,F,G,H\) are the midpoints of its sides. The circle touches all four sides of the square \(EFGH\). What fraction of the area of \(ABCD\) lies inside the circle?
questions.diagram_alt_text: A square ABCD. The midpoints E, F, G and H are joined to form a rotated inner square. A circle is inscribed in the inner square. The outer side length is 12 centimetres.
questions.fast_insight: The midpoint square has half the outer area, and its incircle has radius half its side.

solution.title: The midpoint square has half the outer area, and its incircle has radius half its side.
steps_markdown: The diagonals of square \(EFGH\) are both \(12\), so its area is \(\tfrac12\times12\times12=72\). Its side length is \(6\sqrt2\), so the radius of its incircle is \(3\sqrt2\). The circle has area \(\pi(3\sqrt2)^2=18\pi\). Therefore the required fraction is \(18\pi/144=\boxed{\pi/8}\).

questions.pair_interpretation: Same curriculum area (M1-M5) across different presentations.

questions.question_text_markdown: A time-lapse camera takes exactly four images per minute. Each image uses \(6.0\text{ MB}\) of storage. The camera runs for \(2.5\) hours. How much storage does it use? Assume \(1000\text{ MB}=1\text{ GB}\).
questions.fast_insight: Convert the running time to minutes before multiplying by the image rate.

solution.title: Convert the running time to minutes before multiplying by the image rate.
steps_markdown: There are \(2.5\times60=150\) minutes, so the camera takes \(150\times4=600\) images. These use \(600\times6.0=3600\text{ MB}=\boxed{3.6\text{ GB}}\).

questions.pair_interpretation: Same curriculum area (M1-M1) across different presentations.

questions.question_text_markdown: The cross-section of an arch is modelled by \(y=kx(8-x)\), where distances are in metres. The arch passes through \((2,12)\). A horizontal light beam at \(y=9\) meets the arch at \(P\) and \(Q\). What is the horizontal distance \(PQ\)?
questions.diagram_alt_text: A downward-opening parabolic arch crosses the ground at x equals 0 and x equals 8 and passes through the point 2, 12. A horizontal line y equals 9 intersects the arch at P and Q.
questions.fast_insight: The two roots are symmetric about x = 4, so their separation is twice the square-root term.

solution.title: The two roots are symmetric about x = 4, so their separation is twice the square-root term.
steps_markdown: Using \((2,12)\), \(12=k(2)(6)\), so \(k=1\). At the beam, \(x(8-x)=9\), giving \(x^2-8x+9=0\). Hence \(x=4\pm\sqrt7\). The horizontal separation is therefore \((4+\sqrt7)-(4-\sqrt7)=\boxed{2\sqrt7\text{ m}}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: The intensities of the red and blue lights in a display are initially in the ratio \(3:2\). The red intensity is increased by \(20\%\), while the blue intensity is decreased by \(10\%\). What is the new ratio of red intensity to blue intensity?
questions.fast_insight: Apply the percentage multipliers to the two parts separately.

solution.title: Apply the percentage multipliers to the two parts separately.
steps_markdown: Represent the original intensities by \(3u\) and \(2u\). The new intensities are \(1.2(3u)=3.6u\) and \(0.9(2u)=1.8u\). Thus the new ratio is \(3.6:1.8=\boxed{2:1}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: Each spinner has four equal sectors. The two spinners are spun independently and the two numbers are added. What is the probability that the total is a prime number?
questions.diagram_alt_text: Two circular spinners, each divided into four equal sectors. Spinner X has sectors labelled 1, 2, 2 and 3. Spinner Y has sectors labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4.
questions.fast_insight: Use a 4 by 4 possibility grid and remember that the two sectors labelled 2 are distinct outcomes.

solution.title: Use a 4 by 4 possibility grid and remember that the two sectors labelled 2 are distinct outcomes.
steps_markdown: There are \(4\times4=16\) equally likely sector pairs. With \(X=1\), three totals are prime; with either sector labelled \(2\), two totals are prime, contributing \(2+2\); and with \(X=3\), two totals are prime. This gives \(3+2+2+2=9\) favourable pairs, so the probability is \(\boxed{9/16}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: A 3D printer uses uniform plastic filament with cross-sectional area \(0.40\text{ mm}^2\). Filament enters the printer at \(75\text{ mm s}^{-1}\) for \(10\) minutes. The plastic has density \(1.2\text{ g cm}^{-3}\). Assuming no plastic is wasted, what mass of plastic is used?
questions.fast_insight: Area multiplied by length gives volume; convert cubic millimetres to cubic centimetres before using the density.

solution.title: Area multiplied by length gives volume; convert cubic millimetres to cubic centimetres before using the density.
steps_markdown: In \(10\) minutes there are \(600\) seconds, so the filament length is \(75\times600=45000\text{ mm}\). Its volume is \(0.40\times45000=18000\text{ mm}^3=18\text{ cm}^3\). The mass is therefore \(1.2\times18=\boxed{21.6\text{ g}}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: A positive number \(x\) satisfies \(x+\dfrac1x=3\). What is the value of \(\dfrac{x^3}{x^6+1}\)?
questions.fast_insight: Rewrite the requested fraction before trying to solve for x.

solution.title: Rewrite the requested fraction before trying to solve for x.
steps_markdown: Divide the numerator and denominator by \(x^3\): \(\dfrac{x^3}{x^6+1}=\dfrac1{x^3+x^{-3}}\). Also, \((x+x^{-1})^3=x^3+x^{-3}+3(x+x^{-1})\). Therefore \(27=x^3+x^{-3}+9\), so \(x^3+x^{-3}=18\). The required value is \(\boxed{1/18}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: Six drone lap times, in seconds, are listed in increasing order: \(42,\ 45,\ x,\ x+2,\ 51,\ 60\). Their mean is one second greater than their median. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.fast_insight: For six ordered values, the median is the mean of the third and fourth values.

solution.title: For six ordered values, the median is the mean of the third and fourth values.
steps_markdown: The median is \(\frac{x+(x+2)}2=x+1\). The mean is \(\frac{42+45+x+(x+2)+51+60}{6}=\frac{x+100}{3}\). Since the mean is one greater than the median, \(\frac{x+100}{3}=x+2\). Thus \(x+100=3x+6\), giving \(\boxed{x=47}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: The line \(AT\) is tangent to the circle at \(A\). The points \(A,B,C\) lie on the circle, \(AB=AT\), and \(\angle ATB=70^\circ\). What is \(\angle ACB\)?
questions.diagram_alt_text: A circle through A, B and C has a tangent AT at A. Segments AB and AT are marked equal. Triangle ABT lies beside the circle and the angle ATB is 70 degrees.
questions.fast_insight: First use the isosceles triangle; then transfer its angle using the tangent–chord theorem.

solution.title: First use the isosceles triangle; then transfer its angle using the tangent–chord theorem.
steps_markdown: Since \(AB=AT\), triangle \(ABT\) is isosceles, so \(\angle ABT=\angle ATB=70^\circ\). Hence \(\angle BAT=180^\circ-140^\circ=40^\circ\). By the alternate segment theorem, the angle between tangent \(AT\) and chord \(AB\) equals \(\angle ACB\). Therefore \(\angle ACB=\boxed{40^\circ}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: Let \(x=\sqrt3+\sqrt2\). What is the value of \(x^2+\dfrac1{x^2}\)?
questions.fast_insight: The reciprocal of x is its conjugate because the product of the conjugates is 1.

solution.title: The reciprocal of x is its conjugate because the product of the conjugates is 1.
steps_markdown: Because \((\sqrt3+\sqrt2)(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)=1\), we have \(x^{-1}=\sqrt3-\sqrt2\). Therefore \(x+x^{-1}=2\sqrt3\). Squaring gives \(x^2+2+x^{-2}=12\), so \(x^2+x^{-2}=\boxed{10}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: Sculptures \(X\) and \(Y\) are mathematically similar. The surface area of \(Y\) is \(44\%\) greater than the surface area of \(X\). The material used for \(Y\) has a density \(37.5\%\) lower than the material used for \(X\). What is \(\dfrac{\text{mass of }Y}{\text{mass of }X}\)?
questions.fast_insight: Surface area determines the square of the scale factor; mass is density multiplied by volume.

solution.title: Surface area determines the square of the scale factor; mass is density multiplied by volume.
steps_markdown: The surface-area ratio is \(1.44=36/25\), so the linear scale factor is \(6/5\). The volume ratio is therefore \((6/5)^3=216/125\). A \(37.5\%\) reduction gives density ratio \(62.5\%=5/8\). Hence the mass ratio is \(\frac{216}{125}\times\frac58=\boxed{\frac{27}{25}}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: A rectangular light wall grows in the pattern shown. Each dot represents one light. The pattern continues in the same way. What is the first stage containing more than \(280\) lights?
questions.diagram_alt_text: Stage 1 is a grid of 2 rows by 4 columns of lights. Stage 2 is 3 rows by 5 columns. Stage 3 is 4 rows by 6 columns.
questions.fast_insight: Identify the row and column rules separately, then check the two stages around the threshold.

solution.title: Identify the row and column rules separately, then check the two stages around the threshold.
steps_markdown: At Stage \(n\), the grid has \(n+1\) rows and \(n+3\) columns, so it contains \((n+1)(n+3)\) lights. Stage \(14\) has \(15\times17=255\) lights, while Stage \(15\) has \(16\times18=288\) lights. Therefore the first stage above \(280\) is \(\boxed{\text{Stage }15}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: Box \(A\) contains two gold counters and one blue counter. Box \(B\) contains one gold counter and three blue counters. A fair coin is used to choose a box, then two counters are drawn from that box without replacement. The two counters are the same colour. What is the probability that Box \(A\) was chosen?
questions.diagram_alt_text: Box A contains counters G, G and B. Box B contains counters G, B, B and B. G means gold and B means blue.
questions.fast_insight: Because the prior box probabilities are equal, compare only the two matching-pair probabilities.

solution.title: Because the prior box probabilities are equal, compare only the two matching-pair probabilities.
steps_markdown: For Box \(A\), a matching pair must be the two gold counters, so \(P(\text{match}|A)=1/3\). For Box \(B\), a matching pair must be two of the three blue counters, so \(P(\text{match}|B)=\binom32/\binom42=1/2\). The boxes are initially equally likely, so \(P(A|\text{match})=\frac{1/3}{1/3+1/2}=\boxed{2/5}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: The points \(A=(-2,1)\) and \(B=(6,5)\). The point \(P\) lies on \(AB\) such that \(AP:PB=3:1\). The line through \(P\) perpendicular to \(AB\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\). What are the coordinates of \(Q\)?
questions.diagram_alt_text: Coordinate axes show A at negative 2, 1 and B at 6, 5. P divides AB in the ratio 3 to 1. A perpendicular from P meets the x-axis at the unnumbered point Q.
questions.fast_insight: Find P by taking three quarters of the displacement from A to B, then use the negative reciprocal gradient.

solution.title: Find P by taking three quarters of the displacement from A to B, then use the negative reciprocal gradient.
steps_markdown: From \(A\) to \(B\) the displacement is \((8,4)\). Since \(AP:PB=3:1\), \(P=A+\frac34(8,4)=(4,4)\). The gradient of \(AB\) is \(4/8=1/2\), so the perpendicular gradient is \(-2\). Its equation through \(P\) is \(y-4=-2(x-4)\). Setting \(y=0\) gives \(x=6\), hence \(Q=\boxed{(6,0)}\).

questions.question_text_markdown: A tiny robot starts at vertex \(A\) of a solid cuboid and must reach the opposite vertex \(G\) while remaining on the surface. The cuboid has edge lengths \(3\text{ cm}\), \(5\text{ cm}\), and \(6\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the shortest possible route?
questions.diagram_alt_text: A cuboid has edge lengths 3, 5 and 6 centimetres. A is one vertex and G is the opposite vertex. The required route must stay on the surface.
questions.fast_insight: Unfold the two faces crossed by a route into one rectangle; there are only three pairings to compare.

solution.title: Unfold the two faces crossed by a route into one rectangle; there are only three pairings to compare.
steps_markdown: Unfolding two adjacent faces gives three essentially different rectangles. Their corner-to-corner lengths are \(\sqrt{(3+5)^2+6^2}=10\), \(\sqrt{(3+6)^2+5^2}=\sqrt{106}\), and \(\sqrt{(5+6)^2+3^2}=\sqrt{130}\). The least is therefore \(\boxed{10\text{ cm}}\). The body diagonal \(\sqrt{70}\) passes through the solid and is not a permitted surface route.

diagnostic_model.scope_note: This calibration diagnoses Mathematics 1 only. Physical reasoning is not scored; it should be reported as not_applicable rather than inferred from mathematical performance.
diagnostic_model.weighted_accuracy_formula: 100 * sum(difficulty_weight * correct) / sum(difficulty_weight) over the score's evidence questions
diagnostic_model.confidence_calibration_formula: 100 - 25 * mean(abs(predicted_probability - correctness)), where confidence 1..5 maps to probabilities 0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,0.95; clamp to 0..100

calculation_accuracy.calculation: 100 * (weighted correct answers not tagged as concept_gap or wrong_method) / weighted attempted answers; use observed error attribution when available, otherwise weighted accuracy

time_management.calculation: 0.65 * mean pace_score_per_question + 0.20 * completion_rate + 0.15 * end_section_completion_rate, where end_section is questions 11-15

consistency.calculation: 100 - 12.5 * unexplained_pair_disagreements - 5 * high_confidence_reversals; clamp to 0..100. A disagreement is not penalised when the harder item is wrong and the pair interpretation identifies a narrower skill.

confidence_calibration.reliability: high if at least 12 confidence ratings, medium if 7-11, low if 1-6

reliability_rule.high: at least 4 relevant questions or at least 3 relevant questions with one deliberate pair
reliability_rule.insufficient: 0 relevant questions or more than half the relevant questions skipped

diagnostic_model.overclaiming_guardrail: Never describe a low-reliability score as a stable weakness. Use 'possible weakness' and recommend confirmation with additional questions.

rules_in_priority_order.label: clear_knowledge_gap
rules_in_priority_order.condition: weighted_accuracy <= 40 and relevant_attempted_questions >= 2 and (slow_wrong_count >= 1 or high_confidence_wrong_count >= 1)

rules_in_priority_order.label: inconsistent
rules_in_priority_order.condition: all remaining cases with at least 2 evidence questions

profile_classification_rules.label: Broadly ready
profile_classification_rules.condition: overall_readiness >= 75 and completion_rate >= 0.9 and no high-reliability skill score < 60

profile_classification_rules.label: Strong in familiar problems, weaker in unfamiliar contexts
Needs foundational work
profile_classification_rules.condition: overall_readiness < 45 and knowledge < 50 and at least 4 curriculum tags have weighted_accuracy < 50

strong_but_slow.reason_template: Accuracy is secure, but median response time is above the target range.

fast_but_inaccurate.reason_template: Responses are faster than target but error rate is too high.
fast_but_inaccurate.reassessment_condition: after 40 attempts with at least 80% accuracy

developing.reason_template: Understanding is partial but not yet reliable across contexts.

clear_knowledge_gap.reason_template: Repeated errors indicate a concept or method gap rather than pace alone.
clear_knowledge_gap.reassessment_condition: after completing the topic lesson and 30 practice questions

inconsistent.reason_template: Performance changes substantially across closely related questions.
inconsistent.reassessment_condition: after 2 mixed sets with no repeated error pattern

insufficient_evidence.reason_template: The calibration did not collect enough relevant evidence.
insufficient_evidence.reassessment_condition: after at least 5 additional questions in this skill

strong_and_fast.reason_template: Accuracy and speed are both currently strong.
strong_and_fast.reassessment_condition: reassess in 21 days or after a performance drop

result_page_schema.suggested_retest_date_rule: 7 days for fast-but-inaccurate or strong-but-slow profiles; 10-14 days for developing or clear knowledge gaps; 21 days for broadly ready profiles
result_page_schema.precision_warning: This 15-question calibration provides directional evidence. Low-reliability conclusions must be confirmed with more questions.
